description: Four hooks, each switched by hooks/switches.json (the version's default) and by PLEXARM_HOOKS_OFF / PLEXARM_HOOKS_ON in the environment (per machine). SessionStart runs two: the credential check says so when the guard has no credential, and since 1.6.1 also resolves which `plexarm` MCP server this session will use and refuses the session when that server's token and the hooks' token are for DIFFERENT Plexarm accounts, naming both account slugs and the file the second entry lives in — it makes NO network call when every token it can see is the same string, which is what a normal install does every session, and only a divergence costs a `GET /records/identity` per distinct token, cached for the session; silent when healthy, and it never blocks by exiting non-zero; and the agent sync sends the roster this session can see to /records/sync-agents, which CREATES any agent not already in the account and never retires or overwrites, because what a session can see is session-dependent. SubagentStart names the record obligation at spawn — no network call, no credential, cannot block. Stop and SubagentStop ask the Plexarm API whether this person left work in_progress in this project, and block once per agent if so; they hold a credential and fail open on everything except a repository bound to the wrong project. The record guard is OFF in switches.json as of 1.6.0 — still registered, still shipped, and PLEXARM_HOOKS_ON=stop_record_guard turns it back on. All three credential-holding hooks resolve the token through hooks/plexarm_credential.py — one function, one order, and since 1.7.0 it is: the OS credential store (macOS Keychain, then the Linux Secret Service, then a 0600 file owned by you), and only then PLEXARM_TOKEN. The store comes first because the MCP server reads the store and nothing else, so a hook that preferred the environment would authenticate as a different account than the tools on any machine holding a stale exported token. The plugin's api_token option is gone.
